::: {.lead}
Today you review Lectures 1–14 before the midterm exam. There are no new
ideas: you use what the lectures taught. **Part A** is in Word, Excel and
File Explorer; **Part B** is on a simulator of the interactive page: on
paper, scan its QR code; on the screen, click its link. After each step,
write your result in its box.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Word and Excel.
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Office.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive page, every step has a check that answers at
  once.

## Experiment 1 · Word: headings, contents and page numbers

**The idea (Lectures 7–8):** the styles Title and Heading 1 make clear
headings. Word makes the table of contents from the heading styles
(References › Table of Contents), and Update Table keeps it right. Page
numbers go in the footer (Insert › Page Number), on every page.

**Aim:** make a short document with headings, contents and page numbers.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. In a new Word document, type the title *Our class trip* and give it the
   style **Title**. Then type three headings with the style **Heading 1**:
   *The plan*, *What to bring* and *The bus*, with one sentence under each
   one.

   {{< record "The styles that I used: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Title** for *Our class trip*, **Heading 1** for the three headings,
   and **Normal** for the sentences. The three headings look the same.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Why do you give the headings the style Heading 1, not only bold and a
   big size?

   - [x] Word uses the heading styles for the table of contents.

     Why: A heading made by hand is normal text for Word.

   - [ ] Bold text cannot be big.

     Why: Bold text can have any size; the point is the style.

   - [ ] Heading 1 makes the text red.

     Why: The look can change; the style tells Word that it is a heading.
   :::

2. Click before *The plan* and press **Ctrl + Enter**. On the empty page 1,
   under the title, insert **References › Table of Contents › Automatic
   Table 1**. Then add **Insert › Page Number › Bottom of Page**.

   {{< record "The contents list … headings ; the numbers are …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The contents list **3 headings** with their page numbers (page 2). The
   page numbers are at the bottom of every page.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="3" unit="headings" hint="Count the lines with Heading 1."}
   The document has the title (style Title) and three headings with
   Heading 1. How many headings do the contents list?

   Why: The contents list the heading styles only: 3. The title has the style Title.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-04/sims/toc-builder.html" poster="../../week-04/sims/toc-builder.png" title="Contents Builder: headings, contents, update" >}}

3. In **Contents Builder**, give each heading its style, insert the
   contents, change a heading and click **Update Table**. Why must you
   click Update Table?

   {{< record "Update Table, because …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Word does **not** update the contents by itself while you write: after
   you change, add or move a heading, click **Update Table**.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You added a heading, and it is not in the contents. What do you click?

   - [x] Update Table

     Why: The contents change only when you update them.

   - [ ] Insert › Table

     Why: That adds a new table, not the contents.

   - [ ] Bold

     Why: Bold changes the look, not the contents.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Excel: functions and a \$ reference

**The idea (Lectures 11–12):** SUM, AVERAGE and MAX work on a range. The
part of each day is its amount divided by the total: **=B2/\$B\$7**, copied
down; \$B\$7 stays. The Percentage format changes the look, not the value.

**Aim:** find the total, the average, the best day and the part of each
day.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Excel)**
:::

1. Type the sales of a shop in five days in A1:B6, with the headings
   **Day** and **Sales (JD)**: **Sun 25**, **Mon 35**, **Tue 15**, **Wed
   45**, **Thu 30**. In B7 write **=SUM(B2:B6)**, in B8 **=AVERAGE(B2:B6)**
   and in B9 **=MAX(B2:B6)**.

   {{< record "SUM … ; AVERAGE … ; MAX …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   SUM **150**, AVERAGE **30** (150 ÷ 5), MAX **45** (Wednesday).
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which function gives each result of the week? Sort them.

   SUM
   :   150

       Why: 25 + 35 + 15 + 45 + 30 = 150.

   AVERAGE
   :   30

       Why: 150 ÷ 5 days = 30.

   MAX
   :   45

       Why: The best day: Wednesday.
   :::

2. In C2 write **=B2/\$B\$7** and copy it down to C6. Give C2:C6 the
   **Percentage** format. Read C5, the part of Wednesday.

   {{< record "C5 shows … ; its formula is …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **30%** (45 ÷ 150 = 0.3) with **=B5/\$B\$7**: B5 moved with the row,
   and \$B\$7 stayed.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="30" unit="%" hint="45 of 150."}
   What part of the week is Wednesday (45 JD of 150 JD), in percent?

   Why: 45 ÷ 150 = 0.3, which the Percentage format shows as 30%.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-06/sims/formula-lab.html" poster="../../week-06/sims/formula-lab.png" title="Formula Lab: the Sunrise shop sheet" >}}

3. In **Formula Lab**, do the five tasks. What does **=SUM(D2:D4)** give in
   D5?

   {{< record "D5 shows … JD" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **76 JD** (20 + 20 + 36): the three totals of the shop. The average
   price is 4.83 JD, and the highest price is 12 JD.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="76" unit="JD" hint="Add the three totals: 20, 20 and 36."}
   The three totals in Formula Lab are 20, 20 and 36 JD. What does
   `=SUM(D2:D4)` give?

   Why: 20 + 20 + 36 = 76 JD.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · Files and the practice quiz

**The idea (Lectures 1–6):** a good file name has the date (year-month-day),
what it is and a version, with no spaces. A PDF copy keeps the look. The
practice quiz asks about every unit: files, AI, Word and Excel.

**Aim:** save your work with good names, and find the part to study again.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (Word and Excel)**
:::

1. Save the Word file as `2026-11-29_class-trip_v01.docx` and the Excel
   file as `2026-11-29_shop-week_v01.xlsx` (use today's date). Save a PDF
   copy of the Word file too.

   {{< record "My three files: …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **2026-11-29_class-trip_v01.docx**, **2026-11-29_class-trip_v01.pdf**
   and **2026-11-29_shop-week_v01.xlsx**: the date first, what it is, the
   version, no spaces.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which name follows the rules for the Excel file?

   - [x] `2026-11-29_shop-week_v01.xlsx`

     Why: The date first, what it is, a version and no spaces.

   - [ ] `shop week final.xlsx`

     Why: Spaces, "final" and no date.

   - [ ] `Book1.xlsx`

     Why: It does not say what the file is.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-08/sims/practice-quiz.html" poster="../../week-08/sims/practice-quiz.png" title="Practice Quiz: Units 1–7" >}}

2. Do the **Practice Quiz**: first **All** the questions, then the part
   with the most wrong answers again. Which part was the hardest for you?

   {{< record "My score … ; the part to study again …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good answer: your score of the 14 questions, and the part (Files, AI,
   Word or Excel) with the most wrong answers. Study the lectures of that
   part again before the exam.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   What keeps an older copy of your files that a mistake does not reach?

   - [x] a backup

     Why: A backup is a separate copy: a mistake does not reach it.

   - [ ] sync

     Why: Sync copies every change, mistakes too.

   - [ ] the recycle bin

     Why: It keeps deleted files for some days only.
   :::
